summary: This work demonstrates mechanical resonator-based quantum computing (MRQC) using a superconducting transmon qubit coupled to a high-overtone bulk acoustic wave resonator (HBAR) with three phonon modes serving as quantum memory. A universal gate set including single-qubit operations and controlled arbitrary-phase gates is implemented, enabling quantum Fourier transform and period-finding algorithms with measured fidelities exceeding 85% for two-qubit gates.
motivation: Superconducting qubits suffer from limited connectivity and lack clear separation between processing and memory units. Hybrid architectures coupling qubits to mechanical systems offer dense multi-mode spectra with long coherence times—HBARs in particular provide compact storage with $T_1$ up to 196 µs and the potential for coupling to other quantum systems.
method: A cQAD system combines a transmon qubit ($T_{1,q} = 30$ µs, $T_{2,q}^E = 23$ µs) with an HBAR at coupling strength $g/2\pi = 296$ kHz. Single-phonon gates achieve 94.95–95.93% fidelity via randomized benchmarking across three modes. Off-resonant transmon–phonon interactions in the dispersive regime implement $C\phi$ gates; a $C\pi$ gate requires two off-resonant pulses ($\Delta/2\pi$ tunable, $t_{\mathrm{int}} \approx 2.5\times$ SWAP duration) with a Z-rotation sandwich.
result: Two-qubit $C\phi$ gate process tomography yields $\mathcal{F}_\pi = 89.2\%$ (no-SPAM) and 85.7% (with SPAM) for $C\pi$; gates at $\phi = \pi/4, \pi/2, \pi$ achieve $\geq 85\%$ fidelity across all modes. Three-phonon quantum Fourier transform demonstrates $F_{\mathrm{QFT},3} = 54.8\%$ fidelity; quantum period finding correctly identifies period $r=2$ with clear population peaks at states $|0\rangle$ and $|4\rangle$.
